title: Outstanding Letters of Credit (Monthly Evolution)
caption: Monthly time series of total outstanding letters of credit issued by Mexican banks in USD millions. Shows volume trends and seasonality from January 2022 to August 2025.
notes: Data from account 202401504003 (Import L/C ≤180 days). Represents only a subset of total trade finance. Range: USD 272-678 millions. Integrated from SIMPLE script at user request.

title: Letters of Credit as % of Total Liabilities
caption: Letters of credit as percentage of total bank liabilities. Shows the relative importance of L/C in bank balance sheets. Monthly frequency 2022-2025.
notes: Range: 0.055%-0.123%. Very small share indicates L/C are minor component of Mexican bank funding. Graph recovered after adding total_liab_usd_millions to master processing.

title: Letters of Credit by Type of Bank
caption: Distribution of outstanding L/C across Foreign and Domestic banks. Stacked area chart showing composition over time 2022-2025.
notes: Domestic banks dominate: 98% of cumulative L/C volume (USD 20.4B total). Foreign banks: 2% (USD 445M). Shows market structure concentration.

title: L/C as % of Annual Exports
caption: Monthly L/C stock as percentage of annual exports. Trade finance intensity metric relative to export activity. Methodology: monthly stock / annual exports × 100.
notes: Range: 0.043%-0.108%. Extremely low - confirms Mexico's minimal reliance on L/C for exports. Wire transfers and open account terms likely dominate.

title: L/C as % of Annual Total Trade
caption: Monthly L/C stock as percentage of annual total trade (exports + imports). Broader penetration measure. Methodology: monthly stock / annual (X+M) × 100.
notes: Range: 0.021%-0.052%. Even lower than exports-only ratio. Validates minimal role of L/C in Mexico's overall trade financing landscape.

title: L/C by Top 5 Banks (Monthly)
caption: Monthly stacked area showing L/C concentration among top 5 issuing banks. Identifies market leaders and specialization patterns 2022-2025.
notes: Top 5 banks account for majority of L/C market. Shows high concentration with few institutions dominating import L/C issuance. Comparable to Chile CHL-6.

title: Foreign-Trade Credit as % of Total Credit
caption: Foreign-trade credit (comercio exterior) as share of total credit portfolio. Shows structural importance of TF in Peruvian banking. Monthly 2010-2024.
notes: Range: 3-7% of total credit. Higher during commodity booms (copper prices). Sensitive to global trade shocks and terms-of-trade variations.

title: Foreign-Trade Credit by Type of Bank (Annual)
caption: Annual grouped bars showing TF distribution across Foreign/State/Large Domestic/Consumer-Retail/Other banks. 2010-2024 evolution.
notes: Foreign banks show highest TF intensity. State banks (Banco de la Nación) focus on development/social lending. Top foreign banks: BBVA, Scotiabank, Citibank.

title: Foreign-Trade Credit by Type of Bank (Monthly)
caption: Monthly stacked area chart showing TF composition by bank type. Finer temporal granularity than PER-02. Filtered 2022-2024 for clarity.
notes: Reveals seasonal patterns (export cycles) and bank type dynamics. Foreign banks maintain consistent ~35-40% market share despite fewer institutions.

title: Foreign-Trade Credit by Top 5 Banks
caption: Annual grouped bars showing TF concentration among top 5 institutions. Identifies market leaders 2010-2024.
notes: High concentration market. Top 5: BBVA, BCP (Banco de Crédito del Perú), Scotiabank, Interbank, Continental. CR5 typically 75-80%.

title: TF as % of Annual Exports
caption: Monthly TF stock as percentage of annual exports. Primary trade finance intensity metric. Methodology: monthly stock / annual exports × 100.
notes: Range: 5.5%-15.1%. SIGNIFICANTLY higher than Mexico (0.08%). Peru relies heavily on formal banking for export financing (mining/commodities).

title: TF as % of Annual Total Trade
caption: Monthly TF stock as percentage of annual total trade (exports + imports). Broader penetration metric including imports.
notes: Range: 2.9%-7.1%. Lower than exports-only but still substantial. Shows Peruvian banks actively finance both import AND export operations.

title: TF by Top 5 Banks (Monthly)
caption: Monthly stacked area showing foreign-trade credit concentration among top 5 institutions. Identifies market leaders 2010-2024.
notes: Top 5 banks typically include: BBVA, BCP (Banco de Crédito del Perú), Scotiabank, Interbank, Continental. High concentration market with CR5 ~75-80%. Comparable to Chile CHL-6.

title: Foreign-Trade Loans as % of Total Loans
caption: TF loans as share of total loan portfolio. Shows structural importance in Chilean banking. Series 2015-2024 with SBIF→CMF/IFRS9 accounting transition.
source: CMF (Comisión para el Mercado Financiero) Balance Sheets
notes: CRITICAL: Accounting change Jan 2022. Series spliced for continuity. Jump in 2022 reflects better account identification (11→29 accounts), not necessarily real growth.

title: Foreign-Trade Loans by Type of Bank (Monthly)
caption: Monthly stacked area showing TF distribution across Foreign/Domestic/State banks. Shows temporal evolution 2022-2024 (CMF period only for consistency).
notes: Foreign banks (Scotiabank, BBVA, Santander) have high market share despite fewer institutions. Domestic banks: Banco de Chile, BCI, Itaú CorpBanca.

title: Market Concentration (HHI)
caption: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index tracking market concentration 2015-2024. Values >1800 indicate high concentration. Series adjusted for 2022 accounting change.
notes: HHI range: 1313-1735 = moderate concentration. Top 5 dominate but market less concentrated than Peru (HHI ~2000+). Competitive dynamics preserved across accounting transition.

title: Interbank Foreign Funding
caption: Funding from foreign correspondent banks for Chilean trade operations. Shows external financing dependency. Monthly 2022-2024.
notes: Category: interbancario_exterior. Range: USD 98-1,143 millions (~1-2% of total TF). Chile has access to international credit lines. Graph reactivated after temporary disable.

title: Outstanding Letters of Credit (Monthly Evolution)
caption: Monthly time series of total outstanding letters of credit in Chilean banking system in USD millions. Shows volume trends 2022-2024 (CMF period).
notes: Range: USD 1,873-2,986 millions. Equivalent to MEX-1. Chile has ~4x higher L/C volume than Mexico. CMF/IFRS 9 data only (reliable period).

title: Letters of Credit as % of Total Liabilities
caption: Outstanding L/C as percentage of total bank liabilities. Shows relative importance of L/C in bank balance sheets. Monthly 2022-2024.
notes: Range: 0.081%-0.116%. Comparable with MEX-2 (0.055%-0.123%). Similar relative size despite higher absolute volume. Uses account 200000000 (TOTAL PASIVOS).

title: L/C by Top 5 Banks (Monthly)
caption: Monthly stacked area showing L/C concentration among top 5 issuing banks. Identifies market leaders and specialization patterns 2022-2024.
notes: Top 5 L/C banks: Itaú CorpBanca (leader with USD 23.2B cumulative), Santander, BICE, BCI, Banco del Estado. High specialization evident. Comparable to MEX-6.

title: TF as % of Annual Exports
caption: Monthly TF stock as percentage of annual exports. PRIMARY trade finance intensity metric. Methodology: monthly stock / annual exports × 100.
notes: Range: 22.0%-35.7%. HIGHEST among all 4 countries. Chile banks heavily finance export operations (copper, mining, agriculture, wine). Structural feature.

title: TF as % of Annual Total Trade
caption: Monthly TF stock as percentage of annual total trade. Broader penetration metric including imports. Methodology: monthly stock / annual (X+M) × 100.
notes: Range: 10.4%-18.2%. Still very high internationally. Chilean banks finance BOTH sides of trade flows actively (exports AND imports).

title: Trade Finance Composition by Category
caption: Monthly stacked area showing TF breakdown by category: Exports, Imports, Guarantees, L/C, Third Countries, Interbank Foreign. 2022-2024.
notes: Excludes 'otros' category. L/C appears small (0.03%) because it only includes standalone documentary credits (USD 371M). Most L/C are embedded within Imports (USD 80B) and Exports (USD 3B), captured separately in CHL-7. Top 3: Exports (46%), Guarantees (26%), Imports (24%).

title: Foreign-Trade Credit as % of Total Credit
caption: TF credit (comércio exterior) as share of total credit. National aggregate - no individual bank data available publicly. Monthly 2012-2024.
source: BCB (Banco Central do Brasil) SCR (Sistema de Crédito)
notes: Range: 3-8% of total credit. Includes ACC, ACE, FINIMP, NCE modalities. Aggregated by state/sector/size only (no bank-level breakdown in public SCR).

title: Foreign-Trade Credit by Borrower Size
caption: Annual grouped bars showing TF distribution across Micro/Pequeno/Médio/Grande enterprise size categories. 2012-2024.
notes: Size per BCB/BNDES/SEBRAE standards. Médio: 54% by operation count. Grande: 80% by volume. Concentrated lending. Data quality: 99.5% coverage (834K of 838K valid).

title: Foreign-Trade Credit by Region
caption: Annual grouped bars showing TF geographic distribution across Brazilian regions or top states. Alternative to bank-level analysis (unavailable). 2012-2024.
notes: Southeast + South: 81% of TF. São Paulo alone: ~40%. North: 2.2%. Stark regional inequality in trade finance access despite Amazon potential.

title: Regional Concentration
caption: Line chart showing regional concentration metrics (Gini coefficient or CR5) evolution 2012-2024. Alternative to bank-level concentration (unavailable).
notes: Gini ~0.58 = high geographic inequality. Top 5 states (SP, RJ, MG, PR, SC): 72% of national volume. Persistent concentration over time.

title: Size Distribution Comparison: Brazil vs Peru
caption: Side-by-side grouped bars comparing TF borrower size distribution between Brazil and Peru. Structural differences in SME access. 2012-2024.
notes: Brazil: More democratized (Médio 54%). Peru: More concentrated (Corporate 45%). Reflects different economic structures and SME financing ecosystems.

title: TF as % of Annual Exports
caption: Monthly TF stock as percentage of annual exports. Primary trade finance intensity metric for Brazil. Methodology: monthly stock / annual exports × 100.
notes: Range: 10.3%-23.7%. CORRECTED from 10,000%+ error (unit bug: /1e6→/1e9 fix). High intensity reflects Brazil's export-intensive economy (soybeans, iron ore, aircraft).

title: TF as % of Annual Total Trade
caption: Monthly TF stock as percentage of annual total trade (exports + imports). Broader penetration metric. Methodology: monthly stock / annual (X+M) × 100.
notes: Range: 5.2%-12.0%. Lower than exports-only but still substantial (2nd highest after Chile). Brazil banks finance both import AND export operations actively.

title: Trade Finance by Economic Sector
caption: Annual stacked bar showing TF distribution across top 10 economic sectors. Identifies sectoral concentration 2012-2024.
notes: Top 3: Manufacturing (62.9%), Wholesale/Retail (17.0%), Other (5.3%). Manufacturing dominance = Brazil's industrial export base (aircraft, autos, machinery, chemicals). Graph typo fixed: brasil→brazil.
